# robots.txt report

*Report*

The Search Console report that shows the robots.txt files Google found for a site, when it fetched them and any parsing errors.

**Glossary** (*robots.txt report*): A Search Console report that shows the robots.txt file as Google last fetched it, with a version history and the errors and successes of each fetch. Google said it uses Google's open-source robots.txt parser.

5 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 3 shown or said at the event (2 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [robots.txt report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/6062598).

- [`D1-C140`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Docs: Search Console's robots.txt report shows the robots.txt files Google found for the top 20 hosts of a Domain property, with their fetch status, warnings and errors; to test whether a specific URL is blocked, Google's help page points to the URL Inspection tool and to Google's open-source robots.txt library. `[D1-C140, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/6062598]`
- [`D3-C667`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Docs: Google's robots.txt guide says its crawlers update their cached copy of a site's robots.txt every 24 hours, and that the Request a recrawl option in Search Console's robots.txt report refreshes it faster. `[D3-C667, docs, Google Search Central, Google Search Console Help, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/submit-updated-robots-txt]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C529`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Google said the robots.txt report helps catch CDNs that update a site's robots.txt without the owner's knowledge, and hosts that cloak the robots.txt file, which happens more often than people think. `[D1-C529, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C530`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Google said the robots.txt report uses the parser Google open-sourced at github.com/google/robotstxt. `[D1-C530, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C528`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's robots.txt report shows the robots.txt file as Google last fetched it, with a version history and the errors and successes of each fetch. `[D1-C528, stage, Google, Day 1]`

## For developers

- `DEV-SRV-05` **MUST** · Documented: Rely only on the fields Google supports (user-agent, allow, disallow, sitemap) and keep robots.txt under 500 KiB (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SRV-06` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not put Content-Signal or other non-standard lines between user-agent lines (2 of its claims mention it)
